title_tag: AI Accounting Accuracy: What the Riemann Proof Teaches You
meta_description: AI just cracked the Riemann hypothesis, and it still needed checking. Here is how Indian founders can trust AI accounting without trusting it blindly.
h1: AI Just Cracked Maths' Hardest Problem. Your Books Still Need a Second Pair of Eyes.
quick_answer: AI can now do astonishing work, from proving the Riemann hypothesis to clearing invoices in seconds. But even that proof was released as machine-checkable code so experts could verify it. Your AI-run books need the same thing: reconciliations, controls and a finance lead who checks the output before you act on it.
hook:
A 167-year-old maths problem.
One mathematician. One AI model.
A four-page note that a top expert called "garbled".
And a proof that still had to be checked line by line.

sections.heading: What happened with the Riemann hypothesis?
sections.body_markdown:
On 20 November, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced that he had found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis while working with the company's Claude model, [Nature reported](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-03812-7).

"I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," he wrote.

This is the big one. Bernhard Riemann proposed it in 1859. It is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute's Millennium Prize Problems, with a **US$1 million** reward attached. Fields Medal winner James Maynard told Nature that if it fully checks out, it is "clearly a historic milestone in mathematics".

Here is the detail most headlines skipped.

The proof was published in **Lean**, a programming language that checks every logical step. [Scientific American](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/anthropic-mathematician-claims-to-prove-riemann-hypothesis-most-famous-problem-in-all-of-math/) reports that experts quickly confirmed the hypothesis was coded correctly and the proof held up in Lean.

Meanwhile, the human-readable summary drew criticism. Number theorist Andrew Granville called Alpöge's four-page document "garbled".

So even the most impressive AI result of the year arrived with a verifier attached. Nobody was asked to take it on trust.

sections.heading: Can AI do your accounting accurately?
sections.body_markdown:
Yes, for a lot of the work. No, not without checks.

AI is already good at the repetitive parts of finance. Reading invoices. Matching bank lines. Tagging expenses. Drafting a monthly summary.

Indian businesses are moving fast. Deloitte's State of AI in the Enterprise report finds that **40%** of Indian respondents report significant or full AI usage, against a global average of about **28%**, [according to Deloitte India](https://www.deloitte.com/in/en/about/press-room/indian-enterprises-lead-global-peers-in-at-scale-ai-adoption-across-most-functions.html).

Small businesses are following. A Vi Business study covering more than **2.5 lakh MSMEs** found that over **57%** see AI as a core growth tool and **25%** have already built it into operations, [CXOToday reported](https://cxotoday.com/daily-news/over-57-of-msmes-view-ai-as-a-vital-scale-driver-25-already-deploy-ai-tools/).

But the same Deloitte report flags the gap. Indian companies scored lower on deep AI expertise: **0–4%** at a high level, against **2–8%** globally.

Speed is up. Skill is still catching up. Most small teams have nobody whose job is to question what the software produces. That gap is where errors slip into your books.

If you are new to the tools themselves, start with our guide to [AI tools for faster, error-free books](https://21degrees.in/ai-in-accounting-priyas-smart-tools-for-faster-error-free-books/).

sections.heading: Where does AI get your numbers wrong?
sections.body_markdown:
AI does not make the same mistakes a tired accountant makes. It makes different ones. They are quieter, and they look confident.

Watch these five areas.

1. **Invoice capture.** A wrong GSTIN, a misread amount or a duplicate bill flows straight into your payables.
2. **Ledger mapping.** A vendor gets mapped to the wrong expense head once, and the model repeats it every month.
3. **Bank matching.** Partial payments and clubbed transfers get "matched" to the wrong invoices.
4. **GST input credit.** Credit gets booked before checking that the vendor has actually filed.
5. **Narrative reports.** An AI-written MIS summary sounds sure of itself even when the data underneath is incomplete.

The first one matters most. In an analysis of more than **2,400** product demos run between January and July 2026, **69.6%** of businesses named bill and accounts payable processing as their biggest accounting pain point, [CXOToday reported](https://cxotoday.com/media-coverage/analysis-of-over-2400-businesses-shows-invoice-processing-remains-a-bigger-challenge-than-gst-reconciliation-as-founders-increasingly-seek-finance-automation/). Bank and card reconciliation came next at **14%**, and GST reconciliation at **8.1%**.

That is exactly where most businesses point AI first. It is also where one bad read compounds fastest. Our walkthrough on [AI-powered accounts payable](https://21degrees.in/automating-invoice-processing-rohans-guide-to-ai-powered-accounts-payable/) covers the set-up side.

sections.heading: How do you check AI-generated books before you trust them?
sections.body_markdown:
Mathematicians had Lean. You need your own verifier.

It does not have to be complicated. It has to be routine.

| What AI does | What it gets wrong | The check that catches it | How often |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reads purchase invoices | Amounts, GSTINs, duplicates | Sample 10% against originals; duplicate-invoice report | Weekly |
| Maps vendors to ledgers | Repeats one wrong mapping | Review new vendors and the top 20 expense heads | Monthly |
| Matches bank entries | Partial and clubbed payments | Full [bank reconciliation](https://21degrees.in/bank-reconciliation-the-silent-guardian-of-your-financial-health/) signed off by a person | Monthly |
| Books GST input credit | Credit from non-filing vendors | Match purchases to GSTR-2B before claiming | Monthly |
| Writes the MIS summary | Confident but incomplete | Tie every headline number back to the trial balance | Monthly |

The rule is simple. **AI prepares. A person verifies. Only then do you decide.**

Two more habits help.

Keep an audit trail. Every AI-posted entry should show where it came from and who approved it.

Set thresholds. Anything above, say, ₹1 lakh, or anything new, waits for a human click.

sections.heading: What does one wrong AI entry cost a ₹10 crore business?
sections.body_markdown:
Take a Noida components maker with ₹10 crore in annual sales. Purchases run at about ₹60 lakh a month, all GST at 18%.

The new AI tool misreads one supplier's invoices for three months. It books ₹4 lakh of input credit each month that the supplier never filed in GSTR-1.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Ineligible credit claimed over 3 months | ₹12,00,000 |
| Reversal payable in cash | ₹12,00,000 |
| Interest at 18% a year for about 3 months | ≈ ₹54,000 |
| Founder and accountant time to untangle it | 2–3 weeks |

None of this shows up in a dashboard that "looks fine". It shows up when a notice arrives.

A monthly GSTR-2B match would have caught it in the first month, with ₹4 lakh at stake instead of ₹12 lakh. That one check is the difference.

sections.body_markdown:

bottom_line: AI has reached a level few people expected this year. Even so, the people closest to the Riemann result asked for proof they could check. Your business deserves the same standard. Let AI do the heavy lifting, and keep a verifier between its output and your decisions.

faqs.question: Can AI replace an accountant for a small business in India?
faqs.answer: Not fully. AI can capture invoices, match bank entries and draft reports much faster than a person. You still need someone qualified to check the output, handle GST and tax judgement calls, and sign off the books.

faqs.question: How accurate is AI bookkeeping?
faqs.answer: It is very accurate on clean, repetitive data and much weaker on exceptions: partial payments, new vendors, unusual invoices and GST credit eligibility. Accuracy depends on the checks around it, so sample-test its work every week and reconcile monthly.

faqs.question: What is the biggest risk of using AI for GST?
faqs.answer: Booking input tax credit that your vendor has not actually filed. If the credit does not appear in GSTR-2B, you may have to reverse it with interest. Match purchases to GSTR-2B every month before claiming.

faqs.question: Was the AI proof of the Riemann hypothesis verified?
faqs.answer: The proof was released in Lean, a language that machine-checks each step, and Scientific American reported that experts confirmed it held up. Mathematicians quoted by Nature still called for a clearer human-readable write-up.

faqs.question: Which accounting tasks should Indian SMEs automate first?
faqs.answer: Start with invoice capture and bank matching, where most of the manual effort sits. Add GST reconciliation next. Leave final GST claims, tax positions and investor reporting with a person who reviews and approves them.

ps: The most famous maths proof of the century still came with a checker. Ask yourself who checks the numbers your AI hands you every month.
